The pie chart shows the main causes of agricultural land degradation worldwide, while the table compares how three of these causes affected North America, Europe and Oceania in the 1990s.

Overall, over-grazing, deforestation and over-cultivation were responsible for the vast majority of land degradation, and Europe had by far the highest proportion of degraded land of the three regions.

The pie charts illustrate the number of units of electricity generated from five fuel sources in Australia and France in 1980 and 2000.

Overall, electricity production rose considerably in both countries over the period, and by 2000 each country relied mainly on a single source: coal in Australia and nuclear power in France.

In 1980, Australia produced 100 units of electricity, half of which (50 units) came from coal. Natural gas and hydro power each provided 20 units, while oil accounted for 10. By 2000, total output had risen to 170 units, and coal-fired generation had more than doubled to 130 units. Hydro power also grew, to 36 units, but natural gas and oil fell sharply to just 2 units each. Nuclear power was not used in either year.

France generated 90 units in 1980 from a much more balanced mix: coal and natural gas produced 25 units each, oil 20, nuclear power 15 and hydro power 5.
